en: to be true; to be right

examples.ko: 참다운 친구는 어려울 때 곁에 있어 줘요.
examples.en: A true friend stays by your side in hard times.
The teacher's life was truly genuine.

examples.ko: 말보다 행동으로 참답게 사는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: Living truly through actions rather than words is important.

examples.ko: 참답지 않은 칭찬은 오히려 듣기 불편해요.
examples.en: Insincere praise is actually uncomfortable to hear.
You don't have to try hard to look genuine.
To be genuine, your words and actions must match.

explain: '참다운 친구', '참다운 사랑'처럼 이름에 걸맞게 진짜인 모습을 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 '참되다'는 진실하고 올바르다는 느낌이고, 둘 다 글이나 연설에서 자주 만나요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '참다워요', '참다운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.example: 참다운 친구는 힘들 때 알 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can tell a true friend in hard times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름에 걸맞은 진짜 친구를 말할 때 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical pairing for a friend who truly deserves the name.

phrases.en: Let's think about what true love is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 이야기에서 자주 만나는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in writing and speeches.

phrases.en: I want to live truly and honestly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 삶의 태도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describes one's attitude toward life.

explain_en: It describes the genuine form of something worthy of its name, as in '참다운 친구' and '참다운 사랑'. The similar '참되다' feels truthful and upright, and both are common in writing and speeches. It is ㅂ-irregular, giving '참다워요' and '참다운'.

examples.en: I'm in top condition today.
This hotel provides the best service.
Top-grade meat is expensive.

examples.ko: 시험 전날에는 푹 자서 컨디션을 최상으로 만드세요.
examples.en: The night before an exam, sleep well and get your condition to its best.
They pick and sell only top-quality rice.

examples.ko: 최상의 결과를 위해 모두 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: Everyone worked hard for the best result.

explain: 최상은 가장 높은 단계라는 뜻으로 '최상의 서비스', '최상 등급'처럼 가격이나 품질을 말할 때 많이 써요. 반대말은 '최하'예요. '최고'는 사람이나 물건 모두에 쓰지만 최상은 상태와 등급에 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I hope I'll be in top condition on exam day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '최상의 + 명사' 형태로 상태가 가장 좋을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pattern 최상의 + noun describes the best possible state.

phrases.en: This restaurant uses only top-grade beef.
phrases.nuance_ko: 품질이나 등급이 가장 높다는 뜻으로 물건 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to mean the highest quality or grade.

phrases.en: The weather is the best today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다'를 붙여 상태가 가장 좋다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 이다 states that a condition is the very best.

explain_en: 최상 means the highest level, and is common for price and quality, as in '최상의 서비스' and '최상 등급'. The opposite is 최하. 최고 works for people and things, but 최상 fits condition and grade better.

examples.en: My husband and I made our family plan together.
A couple should decide on family planning together.
There used to be many family planning campaigns.

examples.ko: 가족계획 때문에 아이를 늦게 가지기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to have kids later because of our family plans.
I got family planning counseling at the health center.
Our family plans differed, so we talked for a long time.

explain: 아이를 몇 명 낳을지, 언제 낳을지 계획하는 것을 말해요. 1960~80년대 정부 캠페인에서 많이 나온 말이라 지금은 조금 옛날 느낌이 있어요. 요즘 대화에서는 '아이 계획'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: After getting married, we made our family plan again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어에 '세우다'를 붙여, 계획을 짠다는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 세우다 (to make) to the word focuses on the act of drawing up the plan.

phrases.example: 우리는 출산 계획을 아직 이야기하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: We haven't talked about our plans for having a baby yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가족계획'보다 요즘 대화에서 더 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more natural in everyday talk than 가족계획.

phrases.example: 예전에는 가족계획 캠페인 포스터가 거리에 많이 붙어 있었어요.
phrases.en: In the past, family planning campaign posters were all over the streets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 정부 활동을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about past government campaigns.

explain_en: It means planning how many children to have and when. The word was heavily used in government campaigns from the 1960s to the 1980s, so it now sounds a little dated. In modern conversation people also say '아이 계획'.

en: to be cunning; to be sly; to be fickle

examples.en: He's sly, so it's hard to trust him.
Don't be fooled by deceitful words.
They say people's hearts are fickle indeed.
His attitude turned slippery once he got money.
I dislike the way he smiles so slyly.

examples.ko: 저는 간사하지 않은 사람과 친구가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be friends with someone who isn't deceitful.

explain: 자기에게 이득이 되면 태도를 쉽게 바꾸고 아첨하는 사람에게 쓰는 부정적인 말이에요. '마음이 간사하다'는 나도 모르게 편한 쪽으로 바뀐다는 뜻으로 자신에게도 써요.

phrases.example: 간사한 사람은 힘이 센 쪽에만 웃어요.
phrases.en: A sly person smiles only at those with power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 이득만 따라 태도를 바꾸는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it describes someone who changes attitude to follow benefit.

phrases.en: He asked a favor with a sly smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아첨하는 듯한 행동이나 표정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes flattering-looking behavior or expressions.

phrases.example: 마음이 간사해서 편한 것만 찾게 돼요.
phrases.en: My mind is fickle, so I end up seeking only what's easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신에게도 쓸 수 있고 조금 가볍게 웃으며 말하기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used about yourself, often with a light, self-teasing tone.

explain_en: A negative word for someone who changes attitude easily when it benefits them and flatters people. 마음이 간사하다 is also said about oneself, meaning your heart drifts to the easier side.

t90.ax: Don't be fooled by deceitful words.

en: to be strict; to be meticulous; to be picky

examples.en: Our team leader is really strict.
The successful applicants were decided after a strict review.

examples.ko: 그 집주인은 계약 조건이 깐깐해서 힘들었어요.
examples.en: That landlord's contract terms were demanding, so it was hard.
He is a person who checks everything, so he makes few mistakes.
My mother is picky when choosing ingredients.
The interviewer's questions were stricter than I expected.

explain: '깐깐하다'는 작은 것까지 꼼꼼히 따지고 쉽게 허락하지 않는 사람이나 일에 써요. '꼼꼼하다'는 칭찬이 많지만 깐깐하다는 상대하기 조금 피곤하다는 느낌이 있어요. 비슷한 '까다롭다'는 취향이 많아서 맞추기 어려운 쪽이에요.

phrases.en: Thanks to my strict teacher, my handwriting got nicer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 사람을 꾸밀 때는 '깐깐한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '깐깐한' before a noun to describe a person.

phrases.en: I check the contract meticulously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 부분까지 꼼꼼히 살펴본다는 뜻으로 동사 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before a verb to say you look closely even at small details.

phrases.en: The owner of this shop isn't strict.
phrases.nuance_ko: 까다롭지 않고 편한 사람이라고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the negative form to say a person is easygoing and not demanding.

explain_en: Particular about details; spoken, about a person's checking. 깐깐하다 describes a person or process that checks even small details and does not give permission easily. 꼼꼼하다 is often praise, but 깐깐하다 carries a feeling that the person is a bit tiring to deal with. The similar 까다롭다 leans toward having many preferences that are hard to satisfy.

t90.ax: Our team leader is really strict.

examples.ko: 어머니는 성실한 사람이 좋은 남편감이라고 하세요.
examples.en: My mother says a diligent person makes good husband material.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 어디 내놔도 훌륭한 남편감이에요.
examples.en: He's excellent husband material anywhere.
They say it's not easy to find good husband material.
My aunt introduced me to a decent prospective husband.

examples.ko: 요리 잘하는 남자가 인기 있는 남편감이래요.
examples.en: They say men who cook well are popular husband material.
My friend wants a kind person as a husband.

explain: '-감'은 어떤 역할에 어울리는 후보를 말해서 '신랑감', '사윗감'처럼 써요. 사람을 조건으로 평가하는 느낌이 있어서 말할 상황을 가려 쓰세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 착하고 성실해서 좋은 남편감이에요.
phrases.en: He is kind and diligent, so he's good husband material.
phrases.nuance_ko: '좋은'을 앞에 붙여 칭찬하는 말로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting '좋은' before it makes a common compliment.

phrases.en: My friend is looking for a husband.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼할 사람을 구하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is looking for a person to marry.

phrases.en: He has a good personality, so he'd be fine as a husband.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙여 어떤 자격으로 어울리는지 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '으로' it evaluates whether someone suits that role.

explain_en: The suffix '-감' means a candidate suited for a role, as in '신랑감' and '사윗감'. It can sound like judging a person by conditions, so choose the situation carefully.

examples.en: My younger sibling is a well-known bookworm.
The teacher's room is full of books because they love reading.

examples.ko: 저도 독서광이 되고 싶은데 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: I want to be a bookworm too, but I have no time.
Being a bookworm, I don't put my book down even on the subway.
I heard that author was a bookworm from a young age.
I joined an online group where bookworms gather.

explain: 책을 아주 많이 읽는 사람이에요. '책벌레'도 비슷한 말인데, 더 친근하고 가볍게 들려요. '-광'은 '영화광, 축구광'처럼 어떤 것에 푹 빠진 사람을 말해요.

phrases.en: I've been a bookworm since I was little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이고 더 친근하고 가볍게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that sounds friendlier and lighter.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 독서광이라서 책을 매일 읽어요.
phrases.en: That friend is a bookworm, so they read every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 이렇게 이어 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows how to link it to give a reason.

phrases.en: After reading a lot, I became a bookworm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 책에 빠지게 된 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes gradually becoming absorbed in books.

explain_en: It means a person who reads a great many books. '책벌레' is similar but sounds friendlier and lighter. The suffix '-광' marks someone absorbed in something, as in '영화광' and '축구광'.

en: to be dependable; to be reliable

examples.ko: 우리 형은 말수가 적지만 정말 듬직해요.
examples.en: My older brother doesn't talk much, but he's really dependable.

examples.ko: 듬직한 아들이 곁에 있어서 아버지는 든든하세요.
examples.en: With a dependable son beside him, his father feels secure.

examples.ko: 체격도 크고 성격도 듬직해서 믿음이 가요.
examples.en: He's big and steady in character, so I trust him.
That player looks solid and reliable even though he's young.

examples.ko: 듬직하게 곁을 지켜 주는 친구가 있어서 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: I feel at ease because I have a friend who steadily stays by my side.

examples.ko: 못 본 사이에 동생이 어느새 듬직해졌어요.
examples.en: While I wasn't looking, my younger brother has become dependable.

explain: '믿음직하다'와 비슷하지만, 몸집이나 태도가 묵직하고 의젓해서 믿음이 갈 때 더 잘 어울려요. 보통 사람에게 쓰고, 칭찬하는 말이에요. '든든하다'는 의지가 되어 마음이 놓이는 내 기분을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 듬직한 친구가 옆에 있어서 안심이 돼요.
phrases.en: I feel reassured because a dependable friend is next to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '듬직하다'를 '-한'으로 바꿔 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요. 칭찬하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-한' form modifies a person; it is a compliment.

phrases.example: 운동을 해서 그런지 어깨가 넓고 듬직해 보여요.
phrases.en: Maybe because he works out, he looks solid with those broad shoulders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습에서 받은 인상을 말할 때 '-해 보이다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-해 보이다' describes the impression someone gives by appearance.

phrases.example: 동생이 의젓하고 듬직하게 행동해서 부모님이 안심하셨어요.
phrases.en: My younger brother behaved in a mature, dependable way, so my parents felt reassured.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 믿음이 가게 행동하는 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-게' form describes acting in a way that inspires trust.
phrases.en_equiv: to act in a dependable way

explain_en: It is close to '믿음직하다' (trustworthy), but fits best when someone's build or manner is steady and dignified enough to inspire trust. It is usually used for people and is a compliment. '든든하다' describes the feeling of being reassured by having someone to rely on.

examples.ko: 저는 만화 마니아라서 신간이 나오면 바로 사요.
examples.en: I'm a comic book enthusiast, so I buy new volumes right away.
That shop is famous among coffee enthusiasts.

examples.ko: 마니아층이 두터운 영화라서 팬 모임도 있어요.
examples.en: The film has a devoted following, so there is even a fan club.
My father is a camping enthusiast.
It's a hidden restaurant that only enthusiasts know about.
I started as an enthusiast, but now I'm an expert.

explain: '팬'은 사람(가수, 배우)을 좋아하고, 마니아는 물건, 취미, 분야를 깊이 좋아해요. '커피 마니아'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여요. 영어 'maniac'은 부정적일 수 있지만 한국어 마니아는 대체로 좋은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: This movie has a devoted fan base.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 분야를 깊이 좋아하는 사람들의 무리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the group of people who deeply love a field.

phrases.example: 저는 영화 마니아라서 주말마다 극장에 가요.
phrases.en: I'm a movie buff, so I go to the theater every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 좋아하는 대상을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the thing you love before the word.

phrases.en: This snack has many devoted fans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이나 취미에 푹 빠진 사람이 많다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means many people are deeply into a product or hobby.

explain_en: A 팬 likes a person such as a singer or actor, while a 마니아 deeply likes things, hobbies, or fields. Put the object in front, as in 커피 마니아. The English word 'maniac' can be negative, but Korean 마니아 is mostly used in a good sense.

t90.ax: My father is a camping enthusiast.

examples.en: People called him a dreamer.
I'm closer to a dreamer than a realist.

examples.ko: 이 소설의 주인공은 꿈 많은 몽상가예요.
examples.en: The main character of this novel is a dreamer full of dreams.
Dreamers sometimes change the world.

examples.ko: 몽상가인 동생은 매일 새 계획을 세워요.
examples.en: My younger brother, a dreamer, makes new plans every day.

examples.ko: 몽상가처럼 살지 말고 한 걸음씩 가 보세요.
examples.en: Don't live like a dreamer; go step by step.

explain: 현실과 먼 꿈을 꾸는 사람을 말해요. 놀리거나 비판하는 말로 쓰일 때도 있고, 새로운 것을 꿈꾸는 사람을 멋있게 말할 때도 있어요. 반대로는 '현실주의자'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 몽상가 기질이 있어서 생각이 많아요.
phrases.en: I have a dreamer's nature, so I think a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격 속에 꿈꾸는 면이 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone has a dreamy side to their personality.

phrases.example: 그는 몽상가처럼 먼 미래 이야기만 해요.
phrases.en: He only talks about the distant future, like a dreamer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현실보다 꿈 이야기를 많이 하는 모습을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A comparison for someone who talks more about dreams than reality.

phrases.example: 저는 언제나 꿈꾸는 사람으로 살고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to live as a dreamer always.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몽상가'보다 부드럽고 긍정적으로 들리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer and more positive than 몽상가.

explain_en: It refers to a person who dreams of things far from reality. It can be a mild criticism or teasing, but it can also be admiring toward someone who dreams of new things. The opposite is '현실주의자' (realist).

examples.en: I'm really happy to have met my lifelong partner.
He calls his wife the companion of his life.

examples.ko: 좋은 반려자는 힘들 때 곁에 있어 줘요.
examples.en: A good partner stays by your side when times are hard.

examples.ko: 반려자와 함께 늙어 가는 것이 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My dream is to grow old together with my partner.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 서로에게 평생 반려자가 되겠다고 약속했어요.
examples.en: At the wedding, they promised to be each other's lifelong partners.

examples.ko: 여행에서는 마음 맞는 반려자가 있으면 좋아요.
examples.en: On a trip, it's nice to have a like-minded companion.

explain: 주로 배우자를 따뜻하게 부를 때 쓰는 말로, '인생의 반려자'라는 짝이 가장 흔해요. 일상 대화에서는 '남편/아내'라고 하고, 축사나 편지, 글에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That person is my lifelong partner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요. 배우자를 따뜻하게 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase; a warm way to refer to a spouse.

phrases.en: I want to meet a good partner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼할 상대를 만나는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for meeting someone to marry.

phrases.en: My husband is my best friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '반려자'보다 '남편'이나 '아내'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, 남편 (or 아내) is used more than 반려자.

explain_en: Lifelong partner such as a spouse, warm/formal (좋은 반려자) It is mainly a warm way to refer to a spouse, and '인생의 반려자' (life partner) is the most common pairing. In daily talk people say '남편' or '아내', while this appears more in congratulatory speeches, letters and writing.

t90.ax: He calls his wife the companion of his life.

examples.en: My younger sibling has a lively personality.
She greeted me in a bright voice.

examples.ko: 그 옷을 입으니까 더 발랄해 보여요.
examples.en: You look more perky in that outfit.
The new employee laughed brightly.
The kid who used to be bubbly is quiet lately.
This song is upbeat, so it lifts my mood.

explain: 주로 젊은 사람의 밝고 생기 있는 분위기에 써요. 어른이나 나이 많은 분에게는 잘 안 써요. '명랑하다'는 성격이 밝다는 뜻이고, '발랄하다'는 통통 튀는 느낌이 더 있어요.

phrases.en: My sister has a lively personality, so she has many friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 밝고 생기 있는 성격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person's bright and energetic personality.

phrases.en: The children ran off, laughing cheerfully.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 웃거나 말하는 모습을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게, it describes how someone laughs or speaks.

phrases.en: All my classmates are cheerful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발랄하다보다 나이에 상관없이 쓰고, 성격이 밝다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used for any age and just means a bright personality.

explain_en: It describes a bright, lively air, mostly for young people, and is rarely used for older adults. 명랑하다 means a cheerful personality, while 발랄하다 adds a bouncy, springy feel.

examples.en: That judge is famous for fair rulings.
To become a judge, you have to study for a long time.
The courtroom went quiet at the judge's single remark.
Young judges have started their new jobs.
My older sister has dreamed of being a judge since childhood.
What a judge needs is fairness.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '판사'를 더 많이 쓰고, '법관'은 뉴스나 글에서 판사를 넓게 가리킬 때 나와요. 그래서 '법관'은 조금 딱딱한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: That judge is famous for being fair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서는 '판사'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but 판사 is more common in daily conversation.

phrases.en: The result changes depending on the judge's ruling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판의 결정을 말할 때 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase for the decision made in a trial.

phrases.en: That politician used to be a judge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 법관이었던 사람을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce someone who was formerly a judge.

explain_en: A judge specifically; formal, written term. In everyday talk people say 판사 more often. 법관 appears in news and writing as a broader, more formal word for judges, so it sounds stiff.

t90.ax: What a judge needs is fairness.

en: to be whimsical; to be changeable; to be inconstant

examples.en: The weather today is really changeable.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 마음이 변덕맞아서 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: That friend is so fickle that it's hard to trust them.

examples.ko: 변덕맞은 손님 때문에 주문을 세 번이나 바꿨어요.
examples.en: Because of a fickle customer, we changed the order three times.
Why do you change your words so fickly?
Please don't tease me by saying I'm too fickle.
My younger sibling's mood is often changeable.

explain: '변덕스럽다'가 더 무난하고, '변덕맞다'는 조금 더 거칠고 입말 느낌이에요. 사람에게 직접 말하면 비난처럼 들려요. 날씨나 기분이 자주 바뀔 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 변덕맞은 날씨 때문에 우산을 두 번이나 폈다 접었어요.
phrases.en: Because of the changeable weather, I opened and closed my umbrella twice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 오는 활용형이에요. 날씨가 자주 바뀔 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that goes before a noun. Used when the weather keeps changing.

phrases.example: 제 동생은 변덕맞지 않아서 한번 정하면 끝까지 해요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling isn't fickle, so once decided, he sees it through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 마음이 자주 바뀌지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means someone's mind doesn't change often.

phrases.en: My mood is so changeable these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변덕맞다'보다 부드럽고 무난해서 더 널리 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer and more neutral than 변덕맞다, so it is used more widely.

explain_en: '변덕스럽다' is the more neutral word, while '변덕맞다' sounds a bit rougher and more colloquial. Said to a person directly, it sounds like criticism. It can also describe weather or moods that change often.
